key_insight: DLaR balances exploration and coherence in latent reasoning by adapting stochasticity to model uncertainty and training progress.
engineering_relevance: For mathematical reasoning systems using continuous latent states, DLaR offers an uncertainty-aware alternative to deterministic inference or uniform noise injection.
method: Use Adaptive Stochasticity Modulation to adjust perturbations at each latent step through a confidence–entropy fusion signal.
Use Training-Aware Stochasticity Tuning to progressively decay base stochasticity over training.
Combine both mechanisms within GRPO reinforcement learning.
evidence_signal: Across four in-distribution and three out-of-distribution math benchmarks, DLaR reports the highest average performance among evaluated methods: 27.9%/50.6% Pass@1/Pass@8 on Llama-3.2-1B and 46.8%/68.2% on Qwen2.5-1.5B.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify computational overhead or establish whether the gains extend to larger models or non-mathematical tasks.
paper_title: DLaR: Dynamic Stochasticity Control for Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
